title: Strawberry Rhubarb Crisp
headnote: This warm, bubbling crisp has made appearances at many family dinners.

items.raw: 1 pound rhubarb, cut into ½-inch pieces (about 3½ cups / 450 g)
1 pound strawberries, hulled and halved, or quartered if large (about 3 cups / 450 g)
¾ cup (70 g) old-fashioned rolled oats
½ cup (110 g) packed light brown sugar
½ cup (113 g) cold unsalted butter, cubed

steps.text: Set it to 375°F and butter a 9×9-inch baking dish. Put a foil-lined baking sheet on the rack below to catch drips.
In a large bowl, stir the sugar and cornstarch together first so the cornstarch does not clump, then add the rhubarb, strawberries, lemon juice, vanilla, and salt and toss well. Spread in the dish.

Mix the oats, flour, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt. Work in the cold butter with your fingertips until it forms clumps the size of peas and larger. Scatter evenly over the fruit, leaving it in clumps.

steps.lead: Bake until it bubbles in the center.
steps.text: Bake 45 to 55 minutes, until the topping is deep golden and the juices are bubbling thickly in the middle of the dish, not just at the edges. Rhubarb throws a lot of liquid, and the cornstarch only thickens once the center has truly boiled.
Cool at least 30 minutes before serving so the juices thicken. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

notes.label: Enough thickener
notes.text: rhubarb is mostly water. With less than 3 tablespoons of cornstarch, the filling stays soupy no matter how long it bakes.

notes.label: Frozen fruit
notes.text: use it straight from frozen and add 10 to 15 minutes to the baking time.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: make the topping up to 3 days ahead and keep it refrigerated, or freeze it. Assemble and bake the day you serve.
